purpose: Define where the Director-selected F1A Tight succession may and may not be used before any production motion tokens or app/site implementation exist. Preserve the one-after-another identity metaphor while preventing temporal drag, generic cascade overuse, false product-state semantics and accessibility regressions.

canonical_research_reference.fixture_displacement_status: research reference only; not production amplitude authority
canonical_research_reference.reduced_motion: immediate final state with no scored/identity animation

identity_role.statement: F1A is an identity accent for bounded moments of succession, not a universal transition primitive.
identity_role.meaning: One change enters, then another, then another. The ordering symbolizes continuity through time while all participating units remain peers unless authoritative product state independently establishes a literal order.
must_remain_true: content and functionality are available independently of observing the animation
the onset sequence is visually legible but prompt
motion does not imply completion percentage, loading, priority, causality or data-arrival timing
the moving units remain peers unless an independent semantic order exists
F1A never becomes ambient or continuously repeating motion

allowed_candidates: one-time entry into an identity-bearing brand or explanatory surface
one-time arrival at a distinct stable app-like surface when its content is already ready and motion does not define product state
a small peer constellation introduced as one coherent visual statement
a deliberately ordered brand/explanatory sequence whose order exists independently of the animation
a controlled demonstration or onboarding moment where the sequence is illustrative rather than operational
eligible_trigger_zones.trigger_law: F1A is event-driven, not timer-driven. It may begin once when a qualifying boundary becomes active; it may not wait for arbitrary time, resource completion or provider progress merely to preserve choreography.
not_yet_authorized: routine state-update animation throughout the product

prohibited_zones: loading indicators, skeletons or progress meters
live data arrival or synchronization indicators
notification, toast, warning or error priority ordering
search-result, table-row, feed-item or message-by-message entrance
routine menu, button, checkbox or form-control feedback
parallel tasks that could be mistaken for sequential tasks
any interaction where functionality waits for the stagger to finish

direct_units.reason: The identity mechanism was selected from a four-unit packet; extending per-item delay beyond four units increases waiting and generic cascade risk without evidence.

group_size_and_batching_law.single_unit: One unit cannot express Ordered Stagger. A simultaneous/non-stagger transition may be considered later, but it is not F1A.
group_size_and_batching_law.five_or_more_items: Do not stagger individual items. F1A may apply only to 2–4 pre-existing visual/semantic groups, with all members inside each group moving simultaneously. The grouping must exist independently of the animation; never invent groups merely to preserve the four-beat motion.
group_size_and_batching_law.nested_or_overlapping_sequences: Do not run nested F1A cascades. At a single identity-bearing boundary, use at most one active F1A sequence within the primary visual region.

order_law.default: Follow logical/DOM order, not physical coordinate sorting.
order_law.rtl: For locale-responsive peer sequences, follow locale-appropriate logical reading order.
order_law.authoritative_chronology: If the content already has a product-authored chronological or numbered order, follow that exact order instead of mirroring it for decoration.
order_law.dom_integrity: Never reorder content or focus order solely to make the animation sequence convenient.

repetition_and_frequency_law.one_shot: A qualifying boundary receives at most one F1A sequence per entry into that boundary.
repetition_and_frequency_law.no_micro_retrigger: Hover, focus, resize, responsive reflow, scroll oscillation or repeated clicks on the same already-active state do not restart the sequence.
repetition_and_frequency_law.no_queue: Do not queue multiple F1A sequences behind user actions. User navigation/state changes take precedence over completing choreography.
repetition_and_frequency_law.new_boundary: A genuinely distinct subsequent boundary may start its own F1A sequence if all other eligibility rules still hold.

interruption_and_input_law.interrupted_transition: If the surface is superseded or removed during F1A, cancel its animations immediately. Do not delay navigation or state change to finish the sequence.
interruption_and_input_law.same_surface_retarget: If a qualifying surface is retargeted while F1A is active, commit the current sequence to its final static state before applying the new authoritative visual state; do not stack animations.
interruption_and_input_law.replay: Replay is permitted only in design/demo tooling unless a later product interaction explicitly requires it.

reduced_motion_law.behavior: No F1A animation is created; render the same final content/state immediately.
reduced_motion_law.live_change: If reduced-motion preference becomes active while F1A is running, cancel all active F1A animations and snap to the final static state.
reduced_motion_law.information_equivalence: No order, status, content, affordance or state information may depend on observing the sequence.

held_constant: same displacement per active unit within a context
no bounce, spring, overshoot, midpoint hold or path curvature
visual_mechanism_guard.context_rule: WEB and APP-like surfaces preserve the same cadence. Any later context adaptation must not change onset grammar merely to create visual drama.

before_use_questions: Would a reasonable user infer that unit 1 completed or became available before unit 2?
Would the order imply priority, causality, loading, progress, notification importance or data arrival?
Would removing the animation change what the user believes happened?
Is the boundary identity-bearing enough to justify a branded motion accent rather than ordinary interface feedback?
Can the sequence finish or be cancelled without delaying any action?
semantic_safety_test.fail_rule: If any answer exposes false functional semantics, information dependence or interaction delay, F1A is not eligible at that location.

next_gate.work: Materialize a small non-production deployment-envelope exemplar set using F1A in representative allowed and prohibited/negative-control contexts, pass structural/reduced-motion checks, then present the labeled examples for direct Design Sol + Director adjudication. The goal is to test the use envelope, not to reopen cadence or authorize implementation.

checks: F1A cadence preserved exactly rather than retuned after selection
identity use separated from literal product-state semantics
per-item sequence capped at the tested 2–4-unit envelope
5+ item behavior prevents endless generic list cascades
pre-existing grouping required before grouped batching
input, focus and navigation remain authoritative over choreography
Stage/Character/product semantics not invented from engineering architecture
no production token or implementation authority created
